network.overall_strategy: Use the experimentally demonstrated surface cyanosulfidic core of the Patel et al. arginine sequence. The graph is rooted at 3-aminopropanenitrile, a compact late precursor that can itself arise upstream in the same chemistry, so the network stays within the requested size while preserving the literature-supported guanidination-to-arginine route. Cyanamide installs the guanidino precursor, Cu/H2S mediates cyclization to the hydroxyhexahydropyrimidine, HCN ring opening and sulfur-mediated thioamide editing build the full side chain, ammonia gives the alpha-aminonitrile, and aqueous hydrolysis yields racemic arginine. Only hydrolytic/concentrated cyclization variants are retained; the minimally specified dry shorthand is omitted, and Cu/H2S redox steps are written with an explicit sulfur(0)-equivalent byproduct so the network is atom-balanceable.

reactions.name: Guanidinylation of 3-aminopropanenitrile by cyanamide

conditions.other: Anoxic evaporitic pool; mild concentration by wet-dry cycles helps cyanamide compete with other electrophiles.

reactions.mechanism: The primary amine of 3-aminopropanenitrile attacks the electrophilic carbon of cyanamide, followed by proton transfers to give the guanidino/amidine functionality.
reactions.reasoning: This is the guanidine-installation step of the Patel cyanosulfidic arginine route and is experimentally supported in surface chemistry. Cyanamide is the required synthon for the arginine guanidinium group, although its local availability is a recognized limitation and likely requires concentration by evaporation or adsorption (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cu/H2S-mediated hydrolytic cyclization to 4-hydroxy-2-imino-hexahydropyrimidine

conditions.other: Cu-bearing sulfide-rich aqueous surface pool; sulfur(0)-equivalent bookkeeping closes the redox balance under anoxic conditions.

reactions.mechanism: Intramolecular attack of a guanidine nitrogen on the pendant nitrile closes a six-membered ring, and hydrolytic capture gives the C4 hemiaminal/hydroxylated cyclic intermediate.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) experimentally observed Cu/H2S-promoted cyclization of 2-(2-cyanoethyl)guanidine to the cyclic hydroxy-pyrimidine intermediate. The organic transformation is therefore literature-supported, but the paper's compact depiction does not fully specify inorganic sulfur/redox coproducts. This node uses a mass-balanced closure with H2S consumed and a sulfur(0)-equivalent byproduct; that sulfur sink is partly speculative and could in nature be Cu sulfide or polysulfide (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cu/H2S-mediated concentrated-film cyclization to 4-hydroxy-2-imino-hexahydropyrimidine

conditions.other: Partially dried Cu-bearing mineral film with residual water during wet-dry cycling; concentrated hydrolytic cyclization rather than a fully dry shorthand variant.

reactions.mechanism: The same intramolecular guanidine-to-nitrile cyclization occurs under lower water activity on a copper-bearing surface, with limited water still supplying the oxygen of the hemiaminal product.
reactions.reasoning: This node captures the lower-water-activity Cu/H2S cyclization regime consistent with the multiple cyclization variants reported by Patel et al. (2015), but avoids encoding a strictly dry variant because the minimal inorganic stoichiometry of that shorthand is underdetermined. As in rxn_002, the organic conversion is literature-supported while the sulfur(0)-equivalent bookkeeping is a redox-closed approximation for network balance (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: HCN-mediated ring opening of the cyclic pyrimidine intermediate

conditions.other: HCN-rich shallow pool; transient shielding from prolonged UV favors survival of the reactive cyanohydrin product.

reactions.mechanism: Cyanide attacks the cyclic hemiaminal carbon, opening the ring and furnishing a linear cyanohydrin-guanidine bearing a new nitrile handle.
reactions.reasoning: This ring-opening/cyanation step is directly part of the Patel arginine sequence. It is chemically important because it both linearizes the intermediate and extends the carbon framework, though regioselective opening at the productive site is one of the uncertainties noted for the network outside controlled laboratory conditions (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Nitrile thiolysis to the hydroxy thioamide

conditions.other: Sulfide-rich anoxic pool; rapid onward consumption helps protect the cyanohydrin-containing substrate from side reactions.

reactions.mechanism: Hydrosulfide adds to the nitrile carbon and subsequent tautomerization/proton transfer yields the thioamide while preserving the neighboring hydroxyl group.
reactions.reasoning: This is a hallmark cyanosulfidic nitrile-to-thioamide transformation and is one of the best-supported sulfur-mediated steps in the Patel network. It preserves the functionality needed for later deoxygenation and reinstallation of the nitrile equivalent (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Cu/H2S-mediated reductive dehydroxylation to the butanethioamide

conditions.other: Low-water-activity copper-bearing surface during wet-dry cycling; sulfur(0)-equivalent bookkeeping used to close the redox step.

reactions.mechanism: Copper-assisted reduction removes the secondary hydroxyl as water, producing the deoxygenated thioamide and linearizing the side-chain editing trajectory.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) report Cu/H2S-mediated dehydroxylation of the hydroxy-thioamide. The atom-balanced encoding here treats H2S as the net reductant and a sulfur(0)-equivalent as the inorganic sink. The organic deoxygenation is experimental, but the exact sulfur speciation under prebiotic copper chemistry remains unresolved and copper availability itself is a known environmental caveat (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: HCN/water refunctionalization of the thioamide to the cyanohydrin guanidine

conditions.other: HCN pulse into a copper-bearing sulfide-rich pool; sulfur(0)-equivalent bookkeeping represents unresolved inorganic sulfur speciation.

reactions.mechanism: The thioamide undergoes hydrolytic/cyanative editing that replaces the thioamide terminus with a cyanohydrin/nitrile equivalent while releasing ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) support this thioamide-to-cyanohydrin editing step under Cu/H2S/HCN/water conditions. Because the published shorthand is not fully atom-balanced, the present node preserves the supported organic conversion but uses release of NH3 and a sulfur(0)-equivalent for redox closure. Copper dependence and sulfur bookkeeping make this one of the more uncertain practical bottlenecks of the route (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Ammonolysis of the cyanohydrin to the alpha-aminonitrile

conditions.other: NH3-rich concentrated pool; substitution is written with water as coproduct for atom-balanced bookkeeping.

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia replaces the hydroxyl-bearing center of the cyanohydrin, giving the alpha-aminonitrile precursor to arginine and expelling water.
reactions.reasoning: This amination step is directly part of the Patel arginine sequence. Writing water as coproduct gives the chemically consistent substitution that earlier encodings often omitted. Concentrated ammonia in evaporitic pools would help drive conversion of the cyanohydrin to the alpha-aminonitrile (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Strecker-type nitrile hydrolysis to arginine

conditions.other: Warm aqueous episodes in anoxic pools; two water equivalents are inferred by balancing; product is expected to be racemic.

reactions.mechanism: Stepwise hydration of the nitrile gives an amide and then the carboxylic acid, yielding arginine with release of ammonia.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) convert the fully assembled alpha-aminonitrile to arginine by standard nitrile hydrolysis chemistry. Two water equivalents are required for balance, so the reaction is encoded as a balanceable set with water and ammonia rather than repeated IDs. Under achiral prebiotic conditions the product should be racemic arginine, and accumulation would depend on repeated warm hydration episodes and protection of intermediates from degradation (Patel et al., 2015).

pathways.name: Late-precursor full route via aqueous cyclization
pathways.description: From 3-aminopropanenitrile, cyanamide installs the guanidine precursor and the network proceeds through the aqueous Cu/H2S cyclization branch to arginine.

pathways.name: Late-precursor full route via concentrated-film cyclization
pathways.description: The same arginine sequence begins from 3-aminopropanenitrile but uses the lower-water-activity Cu/H2S cyclization branch before converging downstream.

pathways.name: Guanidine hub to arginine via aqueous cyclization
pathways.description: Begins at 2-(2-cyanoethyl)guanidine and follows the aqueous cyclization branch to the target.

pathways.name: Guanidine hub to arginine via concentrated-film cyclization
pathways.description: Begins at 2-(2-cyanoethyl)guanidine and uses the concentrated surface-film cyclization branch before converging on the common downstream sequence.

pathways.name: Cyclic pyrimidine intermediate to arginine
pathways.description: Starts from the hydroxyhexahydropyrimidine intermediate and proceeds through HCN ring opening, sulfur editing, amination, and hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Ring-opened cyanohydrin route
pathways.description: Starts from the ring-opened cyanohydrin-guanidine and reaches arginine through thiolysis, dehydroxylation, re-cyanation, amination, and hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Hydroxy thioamide editing route
pathways.description: Begins at the hydroxy thioamide and proceeds through Cu/H2S dehydroxylation, thioamide editing, amination, and final nitrile hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Thioamide refunctionalization route
pathways.description: Begins at the dehydroxylated thioamide and reaches arginine by HCN/water refunctionalization to the cyanohydrin, then amination and hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Cyanohydrin amination-hydrolysis route
pathways.description: Starts from the cyanohydrin guanidine and converts it to arginine through alpha-amination followed by nitrile hydrolysis.

pathways.name: Terminal aminonitrile hydrolysis
pathways.description: Direct conversion of the fully assembled alpha-aminonitrile precursor to arginine during warm aqueous episodes.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Strong late-precursor implementation of the Patel et al. cyanosulfidic arginine route. The aqueous cyclization branch is coherent and fits a surface cyanosulfidic setting. Main fixes are to write rxn_009 as mol_014 + 2 mol_005 -> mol_015 + mol_002 and to make Cu explicit in the Cu/H2S steps; mol_006 is best treated as sulfur(0)-equivalent bookkeeping.

Annotate elemental Cu explicitly as catalyst or mineral for rxn_002, rxn_006, and rxn_007.
Label mol_006 as a sulfur(0)-equivalent bookkeeping product rather than an experimentally observed byproduct.

evaluation.network_feedback: Connected 15-molecule/9-reaction network with no isolated subgraphs and strong alignment to the Patel et al. cyanosulfidic arginine sequence from 3-aminopropanenitrile onward. RDKit reports 0 unbalanced reactions, but rxn_009 is only balanceable if written as mol_014 + 2 mol_005 -> mol_015 + mol_002. Main remaining weaknesses are the implicit Cu catalyst in rxn_002/003/006/007, the sulfur(0)-equivalent bookkeeping in those redox steps, and the lack of explicit note that the product is racemic and that Cu availability is a known literature caveat. Good network, but slightly below the 0.9 approval threshold.
